name: Weeping Cherry Bed
blurb: The northwest corner bed, wrapped around the existing weeping cherry at the front corner of the house.
description: A shaded corner planting built around the tree that was already there. Low Myrsine edging carries around the curve, with a Flower Carpet rose, dwarf tea trees, a flowering maple and a run of burgundy Myoporum groundcover filling in beneath the cherry canopy.

name: Front of House
blurb: The narrow foundation strip along the front wall of the existing residence.
description: The band of planting directly against the house front, between the wall and the entry walk. Wheeler's Dwarf pittosporum and African Box give it evergreen structure; a Tasmanian tree fern and yellow wild iris sit in the shaded pockets, and Crane's Bill spills toward the walk.

name: Entry Walk & Steps
blurb: The front walk, the two step-downs and the beds framing the approach to the front door.
description: The most heavily planted part of the front yard and the part you actually walk through. Dwarf Lily of the Nile repeats four times along the path edge, backed by dwarf barberry for colour and dwarf heavenly bamboo in the shade of the entry. Two Flower Carpet roses mark the turns.

name: Locust Island
blurb: The round island bed in the middle of the front yard, centred on the existing locust.
description: A free-standing circular bed around the mature locust, read on the plan as a dashed canopy circle. Golden Breath of Heaven and trailing lantana carpet the ground under the tree, with dwarf New Zealand tea tree and Noell's grevillea giving it height at the edges.

name: East Side Foundation Beds
blurb: The foundation planting along the east wall of the house, running back toward the side yard.
description: A layered evergreen border against the east wall: Gaiety Girl tea tree and African Box for structure, a mass of shrubby Coral Pea and Noell's grevillea in front, and a single Strawberry Tree as the anchor specimen at the far end.

name: Utility Corner
blurb: The service area northeast of the house - air conditioning unit, meters and boxes - screened with planting.
description: Where the mechanical equipment lives, planted to hide it. A single Sweet Olive scents the corner, a shrubby yew screens the unit, Lily of the Nile fills the ground, and star jasmine is set out unstaked to spread across the area.

name: North Side Yard
blurb: The narrow side yard behind the existing pittosporum hedge, shaded by the existing pine.
description: A shady service corridor along the north boundary. Coral Pea and Carolina Jessamine are staked to climb, Pink Breath of Heaven and Lily of the Nile take the ground, and a lavender trumpet vine is staked to run along the fence.

name: East Fence Border
blurb: The long border down the east property line against the existing wood fence.
description: A deep screening border along the fence, and the most varied planting on the sheet. Purple-flowered banana shrub and red barberry give it mass and colour, nine rosemary run along the sunny edge, and eight Tahiwhi pittosporum plus variegated pittosporum close the screen. The existing magnolia and two existing xylosmas stay.

name: West Fence Border
blurb: The border along the west property line, following the wood fence past the existing oleander and ten existing roses.
description: A long narrow strip down the angled west property line. The existing oleander and ten existing roses are kept, and the new planting threads between them: dwarf heavenly bamboo, Delavay osmanthus, shiny xylosma, variegated flax and burgundy barberry, with Coral Pea and blue hibiscus toward the middle.

name: Lawn & Magnolia Feature
blurb: The proposed sod lawn and the specimen magnolia bed that terminates the view from the street.
description: The open centre of the front yard. Most of it is proposed sod, edged by beds that hold the design's feature plant - a single multi-stem Magnolia 'Rustica Rubra' in a 24 inch box, the largest thing specified on this sheet. Dwarf heavenly bamboo, Delavay osmanthus, blue leadwort and trailing lantana ring the lawn.

name: Street Frontage
blurb: The curved bed along Ten Oak Court, the first thing seen from the road.
description: The sweeping bed that follows the street curve, kept low so the house stays visible. Fourteen trailing lantana - the single biggest group on the sheet - carry the length of it, with Lily of the Nile, red barberry and Golden Breath of Heaven filling in. The existing pomegranate and juniper at the corner stay.
